title: Molarity of KMnO4 vs Standard Oxalic Acid
objective: Titrate KMnO4 against standard standard oxalic acid in acidic medium
Recognise the self-indicating end point (permanent pale pink)
Apply N1V1=N2V2 using the correct n-factor for the redox change
Calculate the molarity/normality of the KMnO4 solution

theory.statement: Potassium permanganate is a strong oxidising agent that is its OWN indicator: as long as any reducing agent remains, the intense purple MnO4- is reduced to nearly colourless Mn2+ as fast as it is added, so the solution stays colourless/pale. The instant the reducing agent is exhausted, the next drop of MnO4- persists, turning the solution a permanent pale pink — a uniquely sharp, reagent-free end point.
theory.derivationNote: n-factor: MnO4- (5, Mn7+→Mn2+); C2O4^2- (2, per oxalate ion oxidised to CO2)
keyEquations: n-factor: MnO4- (5, Mn7+→Mn2+); C2O4^2- (2, per oxalate ion oxidised to CO2)

apparatus.name: KMnO4 solution
apparatus.spec: in the burette, to be standardised
apparatus.why: The titrant of unknown exact concentration

apparatus.name: Standard standard oxalic acid
apparatus.why: The primary standard against which KMnO4 is titrated

apparatus.name: Dilute sulphuric acid
apparatus.why: Provides the acidic medium MnO4- needs to be reduced cleanly to Mn2+ (n-factor 5)

apparatus.name: Water bath
apparatus.spec: for the oxalic acid titration only
apparatus.why: The MnO4-/oxalate reaction is slow at room temperature and is titrated warm (about 60 °C)

procedure.text: Pipette standard oxalic acid into a conical flask and acidify with dilute H2SO4.
Warm the flask if titrating oxalic acid (the reaction is slow when cold).
Fill the burette with the KMnO4 solution and note the initial reading.
Run in KMnO4 slowly, swirling constantly, until a permanent pale pink colour persists for about 30 seconds.
Repeat until concordant titres (within 0.1-0.2 mL) are obtained.
Calculate the normality and molarity of the KMnO4 solution.

steps: N1V1 = N2V2 at the equivalence point
Molarity of KMnO4 = Normality / 5 (n-factor 5 in acidic medium)

expectedResult.statement: Three concordant titrations against standard standard oxalic acid give the normality of the KMnO4 solution to within a few per cent, using the self-indicating permanent-pink end point — no external indicator is needed.

safety: Concentrated/dilute sulphuric acid is corrosive — handle carefully.
KMnO4 stains skin and clothing purple-brown — work over a tray.
sourcesOfError: Using HCl instead of H2SO4 to acidify introduces an error, since MnO4- can oxidise Cl- as a side reaction, using up extra titrant.
Titrating oxalic acid cold gives a slow, indistinct end point; the solution should be warmed to about 60 °C.
Overshooting the faint pink end point (it should persist about 30 seconds, not be a deep permanent purple) gives a titre that is too large.

viva.question: Why is this titration carried out warm (about 60 °C) rather than at room temperature?
viva.expectedConcept: The reaction between MnO4- and oxalate is slow at room temperature. It is autocatalysed by the Mn2+ product itself, so it starts slowly but speeds up as the titration proceeds; warming the initial solution gives it a faster start and a sharper end point.
viva.answerLogic: Slow, autocatalysed kinetics benefit from initial heating.
viva.commonMisconception: Thinking warming is only to help the oxalic acid dissolve.

viva.question: What is the n-factor of MnO4- in this acidic titration, and why?
viva.expectedConcept: 5, because manganese is reduced from the +7 oxidation state in MnO4- to +2 in Mn2+, a gain of 5 electrons per manganese.
viva.commonMisconception: Using the number of oxygen atoms or the ionic charge instead of the actual electron change.

preLab.question: Why is dilute HCl NOT used to acidify a KMnO4 titration?
options: It is too weak an acid
MnO4- oxidises Cl- as a side reaction, wasting titrant
HCl reacts with the standard solution
It has no effect either way
preLab.feedback: Chloride can be oxidised by permanganate, consuming extra KMnO4 and giving a titre that is too high; dilute H2SO4 is used instead since sulphate is not oxidised.

duringLab.question: Obtain at least three concordant titres.

postLab.question: The end point of this titration is recognised by:
options: A colour change from one indicator colour to another
A permanent pale pink colour from the KMnO4 itself
postLab.feedback: KMnO4 is self-indicating: excess unreacted MnO4- gives the solution a permanent pale pink colour.

assumptions: MnO4- is reduced cleanly to Mn2+
edgeCases: Using HCl as the acid introduces a competing oxidation of Cl-
expectedBehaviour: Self-indicating pink end point; concordant titres within 0.2 mL
